cards.text: The prophet Ezekiel tells us that in the twenty-fifth year of exile, fourteen years after Jerusalem was struck down, on that very day, the hand of the LORD is upon him and He takes him somewhere. Twenty-five years away from home, friend. I only did a few in a junk drawer, and by the end I was giving the dust names.

cards.question: In visions of God, where does the LORD take the exiled Ezekiel?

cards.text: He sets Ezekiel on a very high mountain, with something built on its southern slope. A VERY high mountain. Me, I have to hop, base and all, just to see over a mixing bowl.

cards.question: On the mountain's southern slope, Ezekiel sees a structure that resembles a ___.

cards.text: So He takes Ezekiel there, and a man is standing in the gateway. One look at this man and you know he is NOT your regular tour guide.

cards.question: The man standing in the gateway has an appearance like ___.
The bronze-looking man in the gateway is holding something in his hand. What is it?

answers.text: A linen cord and a measuring rod
A scroll and a writing reed
A trumpet and a burning lamp

cards.text: Then the man tells Ezekiel, “look with your eyes, hear with your ears,” and pay attention to everything he's about to show him, because that's why Ezekiel has been brought here. I half-listened to an oven timer once, friend, and I'm STILL scraping that batch off the pan.

cards.question: The man tells Ezekiel to keep everything he sees to himself.
Instead, the man tells Ezekiel to report everything he sees to the house of ___.

cards.text: So Ezekiel starts looking. The first thing he sees is a wall running all the way around.

cards.question: What does the wall Ezekiel sees surround?

cards.text: The man's measuring rod is six long cubits, and the wall comes out one rod thick and one rod high. This man measures EVERYTHING. Me? My measuring is a scoop, a squint and a prayer.

Then he measures the gates, one by one: the gates facing east, north and south, and across the outer court with its thirty chambers, a gate into the inner court a hundred cubits from each one. They all have windows all around and palm trees on their side pillars, with seven steps up to the outer gates on the north and south and eight up to the inner gates. And every gate he measures comes out fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide. I've been trying to stamp two cookies the same since before the drawer, and this man gets SIX gates to match.

In each of the inner gateways, by the portico, there's a chamber with a doorway, and it's there for a job. Every room in this place has a purpose. My old junk drawer had one purpose too: holding everything that didn't have one.

cards.question: In the chamber by each inner gateway's portico, the ___ offering was to be washed.
Inside the portico of the gateway are two tables on each side. What were those tables for?

cards.text: Count them up: four tables inside the gateway and four outside by the north gate, eight in all, plus four tables of dressed stone holding the tools for the sacrifices. Then, in the inner court, there are two chambers: one beside the north gate facing south, and one beside the south gate facing north.

cards.question: The man says the two chambers in the inner court are for priests. What do the priests in the south-facing chamber keep charge of?
The man says the north-facing chamber is for the priests who keep charge of the altar.
The priests in both chambers are the sons of ___, the only Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before Him.

cards.text: Zadok was a priest in King David's day (2 Samuel 8:17). Here, his sons are the only Levites who come near the LORD to minister before Him.
Next the man measures the inner court: square, a hundred cubits long and a hundred wide. SQUARE. My cookies are supposed to be round, friend, and some days they can't even pull THAT off.

cards.question: In that square inner court, the ___ was in front of the temple.

cards.text: Then the man brings Ezekiel to the portico of the temple itself. It's twenty cubits wide and twelve cubits deep, with steps leading up to it.

cards.question: Seven steps lead up to the outer gates and eight up to the inner gates. How many steps lead up to the temple's portico?

cards.text: There's a column by the side pillars, one on each side, and that's where we'll leave Ezekiel for now. Don't go anywhere, friend, because this tour is just getting started.

findings.problem: The card drops the date in 40:1 ('at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month') but keeps 'on that very day.' Placed right after 'fourteen years after Jerusalem was struck down,' it now reads as if the vision came on the anniversary of Jerusalem's fall, which the text never says. The joke line also turns 'the twenty-fifth year of our exile' into 'Twenty-five years away from home,' which stretches the time the text gives.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'I only did a few in a junk drawer' adds a length to Papa Dorin's time in the drawer. The backstory only says 'years.' It also plays down the drawer time that his backstory treats as long.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'plus four tables of dressed stone' says the four stone tables of 40:42 are extra to the eight tables of 40:41. The text doesn't say whether they are separate or part of the eight.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The second sentence, 'Here, his sons are the only Levites who come near the LORD to minister before Him,' repeats what card 7 just asked and answered. It adds nothing new. The card also has none of Papa Dorin's voice.
The card is two flat facts with no reaction, comparison or storyteller line. It reads like a footnote, not like Papa Dorin.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question gives the step counts of the other gates (seven and eight), and those are exactly the two wrong answers. A baker can rule them out and land on 'Ten' as the only new, higher number without knowing 40:49.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Seven steps lead up to the outer gates' covers all three outer gates. The text gives seven steps only for the north (40:22) and south (40:26) outer gates. The east gate's steps are never counted (40:6). Stop 1 card 14 had this right ('on the north and south'), but this question drops it.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: About half the choice cards can't be reasoned out from earlier cards and are pure discovery: stop 1 cards 4 (city), 6 (bronze) and 7 (linen cord and measuring rod), and stop 2 cards 2 (burnt), 5 (the temple), 7 (Zadok) and 12 (ten steps). That is 7 of 14, not 'a few.' Some could be set up, for example by hinting before card 7 that the man is about to measure things.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Nearly the whole passage (40:5-49) is building plans, which the docs list as a long stretch that gets one summary story card and never a choice card. The walkthrough summarizes 40:6-37 in one card but asks choice cards about other building details: the wall (40:5), the washing chamber and tables (40:38-39), the altar's place (40:47) and the step count (40:49). Following the long-stretch rule strictly would leave almost nothing to ask after 40:4.
findings.question: When a passage is almost entirely a long stretch, like a temple plan, which parts may get choice cards? Is it only the spoken parts (40:4, 40:45-46), or may standout details like the sacrifice tables, the altar or the step counts be asked? Should the rest be one summary card or several?
